correctness.rationale: Solving the fractional-linear relation in exp(θu) gives Ψ^(-1)(z)=θ^(-1)log((1+αqz)/(1-qz)), with q=(exp(θ)-1)/(exp(θ)+α) in (0,1). For 0<α<=1 the two logarithmic series converge absolutely up to z=1; their combined coefficients w_k have the stated odd/even signs and sum to Ψ^(-1)(1)=1. Conditional product CDFs Ψ^k therefore give valid copulas with uniform mixture margins for every d. For α>1 the inverse is still smooth and H(t)=Ψ^(-1)(exp(-t)) has H''(t)>0, since each log term contributes positively to that derivative; H is decreasing and hence gives a bivariate copula. For the all-dimensional obstruction choose T>max(0,log(αq)). The absolutely convergent coefficients of H(T+s) give a finite signed atomic Laplace measure with mass w_2 exp(-2T)<0 at 2. If H were completely monotone, Bernstein–Widder would give a positive measure, whose exponential tilt would represent this same shifted transform; uniqueness rules that out. This does not rely on the series converging at t=0 for α>1, and the classical all-dimensional criterion only concerns the canonical construction. Differentiating the inverse shows -θH'''(0)=-1414190/27818127 at (α,exp θ)=(100,3); continuity gives a strict interior violation of the necessary 3-monotonicity. The θ→0 limit is independence since q~θ/(1+α) and H(t)→exp(-t). Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 5. An independent exact rational product check of the exponentiated three-dimensional rectangle volume (using generator-coordinate endpoints 99/100 and 199/200) gives a negative volume at α=100 and positive at α=1 when exp θ=3. The supplied script was read, not executed; that finite check is not the proof of the full threshold.
